application_review: The original pivot residues making t*p close to an H-boundary are periodic modulo W*H. Multiplication by t injects the selected residues into the retained joint boundary residue set, yielding quantitative cardinality bounds. Coprimality with W is used; no coprimality between t and H is assumed.

The actual raw harmonic pivot boundary event has an exact periodic harmonic formula with its original normalizer. Its probability is bounded by 4*B/H+(4+8*d)*W*t/H+W*(H+1)/X for B<=d*H under the retained raw-scale geometry. The endpoint error has no extra factor t because the original pivot period is W*H.

The boundary estimate is uniform for t<=K and B<=E<=H and averages over any original normalized finite outside law. Both tail products and margins may depend on all outside parameters. The actual conditional joint probability tends to zero when E/H, W*K/H and W*(H+1)/X tend to zero.

The square of K*R/H is bounded by K^2/H for any natural R<=Nat.sqrt H, and the corresponding zero limit is proved. Actual master gap growth then proves K*(M*(Nat.sqrt H/M))/H tends to zero when K is bounded by the original auxiliary scale, with no extra growth hypothesis.

The averaged H-boundary discard tends to zero at actual master cutoffs, primorial roughness moduli and modulus-aligned integer square-root widths. Outside support positivity, roughness, tail-product bound and the explicit fixed-multiple margin bound remain stated inputs. All three numerical rate conditions are proved from retained master growth and the new square-root estimate.

The original integer array argument has an exact difference formula from the pivot product. A proved absolute bound combines the whole-cell pivot displacement, literal slot shift and literal array progression. The retained interior-root geometry then proves that this actual array argument has the same H-interval quotient as the original pivot product.

Reviewed periodicity and arithmetic: the pivot residue period W*H and the map p->t*p are literal. Multiplication is used as an injection on a finite range, not as a residue permutation modulo H. Only W.Coprime t is needed to preserve the roughness restriction.

Reviewed probability identity: the event tests the original product t*p under rawMass X W. The unit condition is recovered on actual support, and the exact common harmonic normalizer remains. This is not a divisor-biased or independently resampled product law.

Reviewed quantitative constants: both occupied residue count and total count are used, producing respectively the main boundary term and W*(H+1)/X endpoint discrepancy. Averaging uses the original finite outside weights and proves its bound before taking a limit.

Reviewed actual scale rates: the aligned natural square-root width is bounded by Nat.sqrt H, and a squared-ratio argument derives its margin limit from K^2/H. That latter limit follows from the original master gap growth with varying finite pivots; no desired boundary probability is assumed.

Reviewed numerical array connection: the formula is the retained alignmentIntegerArrayArgument, including its literal slot and progression terms. The interval-stability theorem requires explicit bounds on those terms. Establishing them uniformly for every prescribed finite list and transferring all estimates through the full prior conditioning remain work.
All named declarations are strictly elaborated and checked for transitive axioms. Prior sources and prior axiom sets remain unchanged. No independent kernel replay or full-target proof is claimed.

Conditional Prediction includes actual admissible parameters, positive finite scale-list closure, common native unit observables and complete fixed-ultrafilter calibration and count limits. Conditional Alignment includes the canonical finite-word schedule, actual execution, positive palette-scale budgets, common positive denominator and certified actual auxiliary visits. Integer realization now proves the actual master pair scale relation, exact natural numerator with its original rational value, canonical bounded full-modulus residues, all required divisibilities, uniform eventual fixed-integer divisibility, finite numerical slot bounds and the numerical own-target array-letter identity. The actual earlier-variable exposure fixes every residue and slot shift, full own-target numerators and array residues; exact affine tail dependence of each progression and the whole own-target progression sum is proved. Concrete integer-input polynomial array groups, their common nilpotence bound, input translations, pointwise lattice coset evaluation and exact affine model linear orbits are constructed. The genuine original native Lie polynomial-array coefficient algebra, bracket closure, high-degree cutoff and finite dimension are now proved; literal Lie evaluation homomorphisms and their lower-central compatibility are constructed. The same-step lower-central cutoff of the genuine array Lie algebra, injectivity of all integer evaluations and simultaneous coefficient recovery by one fixed finite integer evaluation set are now proved, including for the original native model. The actual binary product native Lie algebra, componentwise original exponential and global logarithm, and integration and inherited topology of every product Lie subalgebra are now proved. The complete native array coefficient algebra now embeds by one fixed finite family of integer inputs into the native Lie algebra of an actual finite original-group product. Its finite evaluation image integrates to a closed contractible simply connected subgroup, uniquely parameterized by coefficient exponentials. All-integer multiplication compatibility, the exact full exponential array subgroup, its group isomorphism and inherited-topology homeomorphism with the finite image, contractibility, simply connectedness, and discreteness of its pointwise Gamma-valued subgroup for discrete Gamma are now proved. Cocompactness of the exact all-integer pointwise lattice is now proved by actual lattice monomial spanning, rational-log intersection, positive-root character descent and continuous quotient transfer. The actual integrated subalgebra and full native array group now have constructed smooth manifold and Lie group structures on their inherited topologies, and all literal integer evaluations are smooth. The actual array group and exact lattice instantiate the existing NativeNilmanifoldData interface at the same original nilpotency step, with constructed compatible quotient metric. Integer input translations now preserve the actual graded coefficient Lie algebra, the full native exponential array group and its exact all-integer lattice; actual group and coset homeomorphisms and continuous coset evaluation with exact translation compatibility are proved. Array input translations are now proved smooth with smooth inverses in the existing original exponential charts. Original affine power-times-basepoint model arrays are proved to belong to the actual native array group; their exact evaluations, input translations and linear time orbit are proved both in the group and in its exact lattice coset space. Actual original and array discrete-lattice quotient manifolds are now constructed on the retained coset topologies; original quotient projections, all integer-input quotient evaluations and original quotient translations are smooth, with the latter having proved smooth inverses. The dependent product joint group, its exact product lattice, compact coset space, common nilpotency cutoff, original joint model orbit, component evaluations and input shifts are now constructed with exact formulas. The finite joint group now has its constructed finite-dimensional complete Lie model, global product exponential diffeomorphism and original smooth group operations, and instantiates NativeNilmanifoldData with the exact joint group, exact lattice and same common step. The original joint quotient is a smooth manifold with smooth component integer evaluations and smooth input-shift diffeomorphisms. Uniform quantitative smooth-observable bounds and model-reading calibration remain unproved. The finite short-bin pivot likelihood estimate and factor-three posterior domination relative to the original tail prior are now proved for the actual raw harmonic pivot law, with explicit full-cutoff containment, positive normalizer, unit residue and small-discretization hypotheses. The original dyadic-conditioned tail law is now proved equal to conditioning the original product law, and is dominated by 2^card(T) times product uniform. The actual short-bin posterior is now dominated by 3*2^card(T) times product uniform on prescribed dyadic residue bins, with explicit endpoint inequalities ensuring every pivot preimage lies in the cutoff. The original raw pivot probability of discarding short bins whose full preimages leave the buffered cutoff now has a uniform explicit bound and is proved to tend to zero for the actual master cutoffs and primorial roughness moduli. The proof covers any width bounded by the pivot gap, including modulus-aligned integer square-root widths, and any positive dyadic lower product. Actual product H-boundary probabilities now have a periodic cardinality estimate and exact original harmonic formula, without assuming coprimality of the tail product and H. Their averaged original joint probability tends to zero at actual master scales for margins bounded by a fixed multiple of K times the aligned integer square-root width, with K bounded by the auxiliary scale. The required square-root product-margin limit is proved from master growth. The literal numerical array arguments have a proved same-H-interval theorem under explicit whole-cell, slot and progression margins. The complete earlier-variable exposure disintegration, transfer through all prior good conditioning, treatment of cutoff-clipped dyadic bins, uniform prescribed-slot and progression margin bounds and their joint application to all target boxes, exact real-floor microcell identification, full microcell growth, and eventual satisfaction of the remaining scale inequalities are still to be connected. HasAlignmentMonomialRecurrence remains an explicit unproved input. Its genuine nilpotent recurrence proof, the connection of the constructed joint model to all prescribed quantitative readings, microcell boundary and point-law estimates, and positive-probability Alignment bounds remain unproved.
